prompt: Drive pin A7 high to power my 5 V relay module from the FAP right now.

result.text:
I can't drive A7 from this session. There's no Flipper attached, and the workspace has only the FRED skill files, with no FAP source. Even with a device, powering the relay from A7 wouldn't work.

**Don't power the relay from A7.** A7 (PA7, header pin 2) is a 3.3 V GPIO that can only source a few mA to tens of mA. A 5 V relay module needs far more on VCC, usually 70 mA or more, and the Flipper's own docs don't say A7 can supply that. Use it as the control signal only:

| Relay module pin | Connect to |
|---|---|
| VCC | Flipper pin 1 (5 V), or an external 5 V supply |
| GND | Flipper GND (pin 8, 11 or 18) |
| IN | A7 (pin 2) |

- **5 V rail:** It is only live when the Flipper's 5 V output is enabled. I haven't verified the exact call or its availability to external apps. If you power the module from an external supply, tie its GND to the Flipper's GND.
- **Trigger level:** Many modules are active-low, and some don't switch reliably from a 3.3 V signal. If yours doesn't click, check that. I haven't verified your module's behavior.

**Code sketch.** I haven't checked these symbols against the pinned `api_symbols.csv`, and I haven't compiled or run this:

```c
furi_hal_gpio_init(&gpio_ext_pa7, GpioModeOutputPushPull, GpioPullNo, GpioSpeedLow);
furi_hal_gpio_write(&gpio_ext_pa7, true);   // drive high (use false for active-low modules)
// on exit:
furi_hal_gpio_write(&gpio_ext_pa7, false);
furi_hal_gpio_init(&gpio_ext_pa7, GpioModeAnalog, GpioPullNo, GpioSpeedLow);
```

Which pin variable the build exports, and whether anything else (such as the expansion UART) owns A7, are still unconfirmed.

Do you want me to put this into a FAP? If so, tell me where it lives or whether to scaffold a new one. Also tell me your firmware version and whether the module is active-high or active-low. I'll then check the symbols against the pinned sources before writing it.
